title: WinRM host spawns a command or administrative process
description: Detects selected command and administrative children of wsmprovhost.exe as remote-execution visibility. This relationship is common in legitimate PowerShell remoting and is not sufficient evidence of lateral movement.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use Windows Remote Management to execute discovery, transfer or command activity on a remote Windows endpoint.
hypothesis.rationale: WinRM commonly hosts legitimate PowerShell remoting, configuration management and support work. A selected child process provides useful visibility, but this single-event rule cannot distinguish an approved remote session from adversary use.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Retain WinRM child-process activity as a low-priority hunting and visibility signal; enrich it with source-session, identity, command and endpoint-role context before using it for alerting.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Identify the remote-management source, initiating identity and child command, then validate the session against approved administration.
steps: Baseline this signal with the responsible application or endpoint owner; legitimate use is expected, and this event alone is not a compromise verdict.
Review the complete child command, account, target device, process tree and the surrounding WinRM session evidence.
Correlate network connections, remote logons, file creation, service or scheduled-task changes and follow-on processes on the target.
Confirm an approved automation, support or administration change; isolate the target and investigate the source identity when unauthorized.
false_positives: Approved PowerShell remoting, configuration management, support and administrative automation through WinRM

validation.expected_outcome: Match selected children spawned by wsmprovhost; do not match normal children, another parent, caller-side WinRS activity or missing parent context.

limitations: WinRM worker child execution is routine management activity. Validate source host, identity and administrative change context before escalation.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
